title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is not part of the 1976 divided-power De Rham notes. It is an upside-down typescript page reused as scratch paper: page IX-116 of Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), paragraph 9.5.6. The archive sticker on the back reads 434.

Setting: S is a trait (spectrum of a discrete valuation ring) with generic point η and fraction field K. E and F are Barsotti-Tate groups over S, and E_η, F_η are their generic fibres. An 'extension panachée' of E_η by F_η is a mixed extension in the sense of SGA 7 IX/VII. It is a Barsotti-Tate group X_η with a filtration whose graded pieces are F_η, an intermediate piece Q_η, and E_η, together with compatible extension data. The functor (9.5.6.1) restricts mixed extensions over S to mixed extensions over η.

To each such X_η one attaches the pairing (9.5.6.2), Q_o ⊗ Q_o^* → Z_{(…)}. It is induced by a pairing of type (9.5.5) defined over the henselisation of S.

Theorem:
- The restriction functor is fully faithful.
- Its essential image consists of those X_η for which this pairing vanishes.
- If char K = 0, so that Tate's theorem on p-divisible groups applies ([33, Th. 4], Tate 1967), X_η lies in the essential image if and only if X_η extends to a Barsotti-Tate group over S.

Remark 9.5.6.3 leaves the extension to a connected regular noetherian base of dimension 1 to the reader.

Proof sketch:
- The first assertion follows from 9.4.6 applied to the components.
- For the converse, suppose X_η extends to a BT group X over S. By Tate's full-faithfulness, the homomorphism X_η → Q_η extends uniquely to X → Q. The text continues on the next typescript page, which we do not have here, to show that X is a mixed extension.

This is the published SGA 7 material on Néron models, monodromy and the orthogonality criterion for extending mixed extensions.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The argument is incomplete on this sheet only because the proof continues on the following typescript page, which is not present.

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of restriction to the generic fibre for mixed extensions (extensions panachées) of Barsotti-Tate groups, with essential image characterised by vanishing of a pairing
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's theory of mixed extensions / orthogonality criterion in SGA 7 IX

ideas.what: Use of Tate's theorem (homomorphisms of p-divisible groups over a DVR of char 0 extend from the generic fibre) to show that extendability as a BT group implies extendability as a mixed extension
ideas.modern_name: Tate's full faithfulness theorem for p-divisible groups

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reused sheet: a page of the already published SGA 7 I Exposé IX typescript, unrelated to the divided-power De Rham notes. Its content is in the literature and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. The text is a typescript (SGA 7 IX, p. 116), not manuscript notes from cote 136.
The target of the pairing (9.5.6.2) is uncertain. It reads something like 'Z_{…S}' (a subscript involving S). Check against the printed SGA 7, 9.5.6.2.
The sheet bears archive sticker '434' and handwritten '131'. The faint pencil marks near 'Barsotti' are corrections to typing errors ('Barsotti' is misspelled in several places in the typescript).
